posts.name: Higgsfield AI 🧩
posts.text:
The grade and the cut ran on the Mac, with no GPU time.

Then have Claude write a check that fails the file on clipped highlights, black or duplicated frames, or a hard cut where a dissolve should be. You only watch a film that passed. https://t.co/bNTTcgUDUk

posts.name: Higgsfield AI 🧩
posts.text:
Fixes are fast too.

Shot 6 came back with a beige rose instead of a pink one. We fixed the colour and had all 140 frames back in about 10 minutes, while the other shots kept rendering. https://t.co/I2FBto5YVu

posts.name: Higgsfield AI 🧩
posts.text:
Then type /gpu in the same chat.

Claude rented 2 boxes with 4 RTX PRO 6000 each, sent over the project and ran one Blender process per GPU.

The boxes started in 40–60 seconds. A 170-frame shot took 13–14 minutes on 4 GPUs. https://t.co/hR8QiMpDuQ

posts.name: Higgsfield AI 🧩
posts.text:
Lock the camera before you rent anything.

Claude built the street, the light and 8 camera moves in Blender from scripts, then rendered a 640×360 preview of the whole cut on the Mac.

Approve the preview, and the GPU run is the one you keep. https://t.co/FrJkM5gFz0

posts.name: Higgsfield AI 🧩
posts.text:
Have Claude measure what the eye sees.

A checker script times each plant from 10% to 90% of its height. Our first growth took 32–40 frames and looked abrupt.

Now large flowers take 115–124 frames to grow.

posts.name: Higgsfield AI 🧩
posts.text:
The growth starts from one sprout, spreads as a ring and then runs down the street.

The delays are scattered, so a single wide shot shows bare stone, sprouts, buds and open flowers at once. https://t.co/dGKzt2PppT

posts.name: Higgsfield AI 🧩
posts.text:
The trick: don't simulate 25,800 plants frame by frame.

Each species is baked once as 96 growth stages. Every planting site stores only a clock: when it sprouts and how long it takes to bloom.

Each solver ran in 26–84 seconds on a Mac. https://t.co/EGQ0vIpWbd

posts.name: Higgsfield AI 🧩
posts.text:
25,800 flowers grow down a street in 40 seconds.

Claude Fable 5.2 grew them in Houdini, then rendered the film on 8 rented GPUs in about 90 minutes.

Here's the workflow, with the prompts to make your own: https://t.co/aDhzauO4xI
